reason: The ceiling is overstated about 10-50x, and the evidence mostly does not support the mechanism. (1) 6bba holds 1,740 of the 1,907 a_never FN (fn_anatomy_exp39.md) and 91% of the idea's ceiling, yet v2 measured that 6bba misses are not a merge problem: close GT pairs under 7 um are only 1% of missed nodes, and their density is the same as for matched nodes. The nearest raw peak sits at |dz| median 4.9 um and dxy median 6.8 um, and only 42% of offsets are z-dominant. Only 4% of the 326 misses at 7-10 um show an intensity valley (wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md l.5-8). The idea's guess of 1/3 of 1,740 = 580 FN has no measured support; about 5-10% is the defensible share. (2) The attract3 evidence (preds +0.55..+1.0 um farther apart than GT) comes from pairs where BOTH GT nodes are matched under 3 um to DISTINCT preds. The critic says explicitly that this selection drops merged pairs (r2_critic.notes.md l.18). It is a repulsion bias of detected pairs, not a merged-pair signature, and adding nodes does not act on it. (3) The 44b6 under-segmentation finding (Ultrack pt 2.3 um from the missed GT; our node 1.9 um from another Ultrack pt about 7 um away) is real but small: 167 FN = +0.0012 at most. It was measured on 25 of 63 placed clips of ONE recording, and 22-25% of 44b6 FN sit in overlapping multi-copy crops. Its typical separation (about 7 um) lies in dogrescue's band already. The increment in the 4.5-6.5 um band is about a third of it. (4) Geometry: the candidate is placed at the node's xy (plus or minus 1.6 um recentring), so a missed GT at dxy of about 6.8 um from the node cannot be matched. Only the z-dominant, small-dxy subset can be reached. (5) Hole valley statistics in exactly this band: holes 4-5 um are under 0.85 in 1.2% and under 0.95 in 4.7% (n=169); holes 5-6 um are 0% and 5.3% (n=132) (r1_research_hole-fill-sandwich.notes.md l.13). Meanwhile 97% of same-frame raw-peak pairs under 5 um are z-stacked duplicates of one nucleus (r1_hyp_detection l.14), so the triggered set is small and dominated by false splits. (6) Structural cap inherited from the dogrescue track assembly: standalone tracks of 6 or more frames convert only the internal edges of miss runs, about 300 of 1,907 a_never FN (16%). Boundary edges stay FN. Even the idea's own +0.005 times 0.16 gives +0.0008. Recomputed increment over dogrescue: 44b6 167 x 0.5 (distinct nucleus) x 0.35 (4.5-6.5 um band) x 0.5 (z-dominant) is about 15 FN. 6bba 1,740 x 0.05-0.10 x 0.5 is about 45-90 FN. Multiplied by 0.16-0.4 for runs that survive min_len 6, that leaves about 10-40 FN, or +0.0001..+0.0003 lab gross. Node cost: breakeven is 0.093 x annotated fraction edges per added node, about 1 edge per 77 nodes in 6bba and 1 per 1,000 in 44b6. Real splits pay, but false splits of z-elongated nuclei add nodes and create competitors for the 7.9k GT nodes in the 4-7 um swap zone. That puts net lab at about -0.0003..+0.0003. Transfer: the statistic is image-based, not network confidence, so it has no in-sample leak and is the one point in the idea's favour. But the pool was measured on the exp39 base, not x138 (whose head, readmit and gap filler move and add nodes), and the only positive evidence comes from one recording (44b6/dorado). Public gain is about +0.0000..+0.0005, far below the +0.002 bar and the 0.003 LB noise. It also rides on dogrescue, which was refuted on value (v_localisation-training-free_dog-missing-track-rescue_value.json), so its probe slot and infrastructure are unlikely to exist.
fix_if_any: It cannot be repaired to reach +0.002 public; at best it is a +0.0003 add-on. If the team still wants it, fold it into a desk test that needs no build (about 1 h on friend A's machine, CPU, raw zarr plus exp39 or x138 final graphs). For every a_never GT node in 24 videos (12 of 44b6, 12 of 6bba), compute the z-profile at the nearest final node's xy. Count the nodes where the rule would place a candidate within 3 um of the GT, and the FALSE trigger rate over all final nodes in frames with NN distance under 8 um. Proceed only if at least 1.5 annotated a_never hits per 100 triggered nodes AND hits scale to at least 150 FN over 199 videos AND those hits sit in runs of 6 or more (internal edges). Otherwise drop it. The one version with more headroom is to attach z-split candidates to open track ends (converting boundary edges too) or to feed them as extra ILP candidates. That is readmit/gapfill territory, LB-neutral in v2, and would need the x138 stack re-run, which does not fit the deadline.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0000..+0.0005. Central guess +0.0001, inside LB noise (0.003). Downside about -0.0005 if false z-splits of elongated nuclei fill the shared node cap and steal swap-zone matches.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0000..+0.0008. Central guess +0.0002. Dense unseen embryos with real z-stacked under-segmentation could gain a little more, but the ≥6-frame standalone-track structure caps it the same way. Downside is bounded by the node cap at about -0.0005..-0.001.
critical_path: It depends on dogrescue: agent adds DOGRESCUE_ZSPLIT to tools/dog_rescue.py (Sat 26, about 1.5 h) -> friend A runs the controls on 12-24 videos plus the increment inside the dogrescue selection and confirmation grid (Sat-Sun, about 2 h CPU on the 5070 Ti machine) -> the lab gate fails with P ~0.9, and dogrescue itself is refuted -> no LB slot. A standalone probe would need its own kernel build plus a slot on Mon 28 Sep (scored about 28 Sep 18:00 UTC at the earliest). That is technically possible, but P(scored AND passing the gate) is well under 70%, and a visible LB effect is under 10%.
